exact_items: The canonical vocabulary is: `primary_view` (full primary-content destinations: Dashboard, Projects, Wizard, Interview, Settings, Usage, Orchestrator); `side_panel` (activity-bar panel destinations: chat, files, source_control, github_actions, docker_manager, artifacts, run_debug); `bottom_panel` (bottom shell destinations: terminal, problems, output, ports, browser, debug); `embedded_surface` (embedded sub-surfaces: document_pane, agent_activity); `page_tab` (tab within a routed page: Orchestrator tabs)
Keep destination-local refinements outside the enum and outside the base route contract.
Use `page_tab` when the routed destination must land inside a known page and force a specific tab.
What is not `target_kind`: docked vs floating; panel width; widget slot; subview id; repo/worktree selection; browser tab id; workspace tab id
notes: target_kind is destination class only — not shell state, not object taxonomy. workspace_tab_id and browser_tab_id are NOT target_kind values. page_tab is the value for Orchestrator and similar multi-tab pages, and must remain general — not renamed around one page.

exact_items: The canonical selector rule is: exactly one primary selector is present: `subject_id` OR `object_kind` + `object_id`
`tab_id`, `focused_run_id`, `thread_id`, and `inspector_target` never replace primary selector identity.
`project_id` is required scope, not selector identity.

Resolution order: (1) restore project_id, (2) restore route scope (focused_run_id, thread_id), (3) restore destination class from target_kind, (4) resolve primary selector (subject_id OR object_kind+object_id), (5) apply narrow focus refinement (tab_id, inspector_target)
Reject multi-selector route payloads as non-canonical. Normalize all special-case ids into `subject_id` or `object_kind` + `object_id` before they enter the canonical route layer.
canonical_replacement_hints: object_kind + object_id for all listed special-case IDs
notes: One route, one primary selector. wizard_step is sub-selection (not a primary selector). usage_event_ref must normalize into object_kind=usage_event + object_id. resume_url flows still encode wizard-step more concretely than the general contract — this must be reconciled.

exact_items: `resume_url` must stay narrower than the internal route contract.
The serialized form carries: stable primary selector identity; required scope when needed; narrow anchor detail when the flow requires it
The serialized form does not carry: shell layout state; panel widths; widget state; broad filter state; provider/account disclosure data
`resume_url` decodes into `route_target`. `resume_url` does not define a second routing ontology.

Good serialized fields: `project_id`; `subject_id` or `object_kind` + `object_id`; `thread_id` when thread scope is required; `focused_run_id` when run scope is required; narrow anchor detail such as wizard-step focus when the workflow requires exact resumption
Define `resume_url` as serialized `route_target` transport in `Contracts_V0.md`. State the allowed serialized data classes directly.
stale_tokens: resume_url stronger than general route contract
notes: resume_url is transport, route_target is canonical identity. Serialization must stay narrower than the internal route model. Wizard step detail is a narrow serialized anchor, not a new top-level base route field. Remove resume_url's implicit status as the strongest navigation mechanism once Contracts_V0 defines route_target.
